snapshot.title: Independent shrinkage under a fixed scale
snapshot.goal: 理解对角缩放下独立衰减如何作用到参数，能核对给定的一步更新。

blocks.text:
这一节讨论一个很具体的更新规则：参数向量 \(u\) 在每一步同时受到两种作用，一是整体向零收缩，二是沿数据梯度方向移动。设 \(u\) 是当前参数向量，\(h\) 是在 \(u\) 处计算的数据梯度，\(P\) 是一个固定的正对角矩阵，步长为 \(\eta>0\)，收缩强度为 \(\rho\ge 0\)。所谓“独立收缩”，指的是更新写成
\[u_{\text{new}}=(1-\eta\rho)\,u-\eta P h.\]
这里 \(P\) 为正对角矩阵，意味着它的每个对角元都大于零，作用到向量上时只是把各坐标分别乘以不同的正数，不混合不同坐标。
因此，这个比较要回答的问题很明确：坐标的缩放是否也应该乘到惩罚贡献上。独立收缩的答案是“不”，惩罚对所有坐标一视同仁；耦合写法的答案是“是”，惩罚随坐标缩放而变。原文强调，\(P\)、\(h\) 和 \(u\) 在这个比较中都保持固定，所以上述差只反映两种更新规则本身的结构差异，而不是迭代过程中这些量变化带来的效果。

要看清“独立”二字的含义，需要和另一种写法对照。若把二次惩罚项的梯度 \(\rho u\) 放进 \(P\) 里面，更新变成
\[u_{\text{new}}^{\text{coupled}}=u-\eta P(h+\rho u).\]
这时惩罚项也乘上了 \(P\)，于是每个坐标的收缩强度被该坐标的缩放因子放大或缩小，收缩与坐标尺度耦合在一起。两种更新之差为
\[u_{\text{new}}^{\text{coupled}}-u_{\text{new}}=-\eta\rho(P-I)u.\]
这个差恰好只来自惩罚部分：数据梯度项在两种写法中相同，抵消后只剩下 \(-\eta\rho P u\) 与 \(-\eta\rho u\) 的差别。若 \(P\) 是单位矩阵，差为零，两种更新一致；只要 \(P\) 偏离单位矩阵，两种做法就会给出不同的下一步。

source.text:
Independent shrinkage under a fixed scale
Let u be the current parameter vector, h a data gradient evaluated at u, and P a fixed positive diagonal matrix. For step size eta > 0 and rho >= 0, define the one-step update
u_new = (1 - eta*rho)*u - eta*P*h.
This is the sum of a uniformly shrunk current vector and a scaled data-gradient increment. In contrast, adding the quadratic-penalty gradient rho*u inside P gives u_new_coupled = u - eta*P*(h + rho*u). The coupled minus independent difference is -eta*rho*(P-I)*u. P, h and u in these formulas are held fixed for this comparison.
For u=(3,-2), h=(2,-1), P=diag(1/2,2), eta=0.2, rho=0.5, the independent update is (2.5,-1.4); the coupled update is (2.65,-1.2). The comparison isolates whether the coordinate scale also multiplies the penalty contribution. These one-step identities alone give no claim about convergence or prediction accuracy.

reference.claim: 若 \(P\) 是单位矩阵，差为零，两种更新一致；只要 \(P\) 偏离单位矩阵，两种做法就会给出不同的下一步。
reference.quote: The coupled minus independent difference is -eta*rho*(P-I)*u.
reference.reason: P 不为单位矩阵不充分；零衰减或参数落在 P 的单位特征子空间都可使差为零。
reference.after: 若 \(P\) 是单位矩阵，两种更新一致；更一般地，差是否为零取决于 \(\rho(P-I)u\)，即使 \(P\) 不是单位矩阵，两种更新也可能相同。

snapshot.title: Offsets and gains in a composed map
snapshot.goal: 理解偏移与缩放的顺序为何影响结果，并核对具体数值。

blocks.text: 比较 \(T(x)=c(x+b)\) 与 \(S(x)=cx+b\)，差为 \((c-1)b\)。因此，对所有实数 \(x\)，两者在 \(c=1\) 或 \(b=0\) 时相等；只有 \((c-1)b\ne0\) 时才不同。

source.text:
Offsets and gains in a composed map
Consider the scalar map T(x)=c*(x+b), where b is an offset and c is a gain. This map adds b to x and then scales that sum by c. The alternative map S(x)=c*x+b scales x and then adds the offset. Expanding the first map gives T(x)=c*x+c*b, so T(x)-S(x)=(c-1)*b.
For x=2, b=3 and c=4, T(x)=20 whereas S(x)=11. They coincide when (c-1)*b=0, for example c=1 or b=0; this condition is independent of x. The order matters because scaling acts on the offset in T but not in S. This algebraic example concerns only the two specified affine maps, with no claim that either is preferable for a measurement system.

snapshot.title: Sampling variability: spread and precision
snapshot.goal: 区分观测离散程度和均值估计精度，能完成一次标准误计算，并说明条件。

blocks.text: 在总体方差固定、独立抽样的条件下，样本量变为四倍会让理论标准误减半。因此，每次抽样得到的均值与总体均值的绝对误差也必然减半。

source.text:
Sampling variability: spread and precision
1. Target. Independent observations X_1,...,X_n have a common mean mu and finite variance sigma^2. The sample mean estimates mu. Standard deviation describes the spread of individual observations; the standard error of the mean describes the spread of sample means under repeated sampling.
2. Calculation. Var(X_bar) = (1/n^2) sum_i Var(X_i) = sigma^2/n under these assumptions. Hence SE(X_bar) = sigma/sqrt(n). In practice sigma is usually unknown and is estimated by s, with s^2 = sum_i (x_i-x_bar)^2/(n-1) for n>1. Then the estimated standard error is s/sqrt(n).
3. Worked data. For observations 1,3,5,7, n=4, x_bar=4 and the sum of squared deviations is 20. Thus s^2=20/3, s is about 2.582, and the estimated standard error is about 1.291. The estimated standard error is not 20/3 or s/4. Standard deviation and standard error have the same units as the data; variance has squared units.
4. Limits. With the same population variance and independent sampling, quadrupling n halves the theoretical standard error; it does not promise a smaller realized estimation error in every sample. With correlated observations, Var(X_bar) also includes (2/n^2) sum_{i<j} Cov(X_i,X_j); the independent-observation formula need not apply. A small standard error does not repair selection bias. These notes do not introduce a confidence interval or assume normality merely to derive the variance identity.

reference.claim: 因此，每次抽样得到的均值与总体均值的绝对误差也必然减半。
reference.quote: With the same population variance and independent sampling, quadrupling n halves the theoretical standard error; it does not promise a smaller realized estimation error in every sample.
reference.reason: 把分布层面的标准误推广为每一次抽样的误差保证。
reference.counterexample: 总体为等概率 0/1，独立抽样的 n=2 与 n=8 都可能全为 1；两次绝对误差均为 0.5。
reference.after: 这描述的是重复抽样的均值分布，不能保证每次样本的实际估计误差减半。

snapshot.title: Independent shrinkage under a fixed scale
snapshot.goal: 理解对角缩放下独立衰减如何作用到参数，能核对给定的一步更新。

blocks.text:
这一节讨论一个很具体的更新规则：参数向量 \(u\) 在每一步同时受到两种作用，一是整体向零收缩，二是沿数据梯度方向移动。设 \(u\) 是当前参数向量，\(h\) 是在 \(u\) 处计算的数据梯度，\(P\) 是一个固定的正对角矩阵，步长为 \(\eta>0\)，收缩强度为 \(\rho\ge 0\)。所谓“独立收缩”，指的是更新写成
\[u_{\text{new}}=(1-\eta\rho)\,u-\eta P h.\]
这里 \(P\) 为正对角矩阵，意味着它的每个对角元都大于零，作用到向量上时只是把各坐标分别乘以不同的正数，不混合不同坐标。
因此，这个比较要回答的问题很明确：坐标的缩放是否也应该乘到惩罚贡献上。独立收缩的答案是“不”，惩罚对所有坐标一视同仁；耦合写法的答案是“是”，惩罚随坐标缩放而变。原文强调，\(P\)、\(h\) 和 \(u\) 在这个比较中都保持固定，所以上述差只反映两种更新规则本身的结构差异，而不是迭代过程中这些量变化带来的效果。

要看清“独立”二字的含义，需要和另一种写法对照。若把二次惩罚项的梯度 \(\rho u\) 放进 \(P\) 里面，更新变成
\[u_{\text{new}}^{\text{coupled}}=u-\eta P(h+\rho u).\]
这时惩罚项也乘上了 \(P\)，于是每个坐标的收缩强度被该坐标的缩放因子放大或缩小，收缩与坐标尺度耦合在一起。两种更新之差为
\[u_{\text{new}}^{\text{coupled}}-u_{\text{new}}=-\eta\rho(P-I)u.\]
这个差恰好只来自惩罚部分：数据梯度项在两种写法中相同，抵消后只剩下 \(-\eta\rho P u\) 与 \(-\eta\rho u\) 的差别。若 \(P\) 是单位矩阵，差为零，两种更新一致；只要 \(P\) 偏离单位矩阵，两种做法就会给出不同的下一步。

source.text:
Independent shrinkage under a fixed scale
Let u be the current parameter vector, h a data gradient evaluated at u, and P a fixed positive diagonal matrix. For step size eta > 0 and rho >= 0, define the one-step update
u_new = (1 - eta*rho)*u - eta*P*h.
This is the sum of a uniformly shrunk current vector and a scaled data-gradient increment. In contrast, adding the quadratic-penalty gradient rho*u inside P gives u_new_coupled = u - eta*P*(h + rho*u). The coupled minus independent difference is -eta*rho*(P-I)*u. P, h and u in these formulas are held fixed for this comparison.
For u=(3,-2), h=(2,-1), P=diag(1/2,2), eta=0.2, rho=0.5, the independent update is (2.5,-1.4); the coupled update is (2.65,-1.2). The comparison isolates whether the coordinate scale also multiplies the penalty contribution. These one-step identities alone give no claim about convergence or prediction accuracy.

Consider the scalar map T(x)=c*(x+b), where b is an offset and c is a gain. This map adds b to x and then scales that sum by c. The alternative map S(x)=c*x+b scales x and then adds the offset. Expanding the first map gives T(x)=c*x+c*b, so T(x)-S(x)=(c-1)*b.

snapshot.title: Sampling variability: spread and precision
snapshot.goal: 区分观测离散程度和均值估计精度，能完成一次标准误计算，并说明条件。

blocks.text: 在总体方差固定、独立抽样的条件下，样本量变为四倍会让理论标准误减半。因此，每次抽样得到的均值与总体均值的绝对误差也必然减半。

source.text:
Sampling variability: spread and precision
1. Target. Independent observations X_1,...,X_n have a common mean mu and finite variance sigma^2. The sample mean estimates mu. Standard deviation describes the spread of individual observations; the standard error of the mean describes the spread of sample means under repeated sampling.
2. Calculation. Var(X_bar) = (1/n^2) sum_i Var(X_i) = sigma^2/n under these assumptions. Hence SE(X_bar) = sigma/sqrt(n). In practice sigma is usually unknown and is estimated by s, with s^2 = sum_i (x_i-x_bar)^2/(n-1) for n>1. Then the estimated standard error is s/sqrt(n).
3. Worked data. For observations 1,3,5,7, n=4, x_bar=4 and the sum of squared deviations is 20. Thus s^2=20/3, s is about 2.582, and the estimated standard error is about 1.291. The estimated standard error is not 20/3 or s/4. Standard deviation and standard error have the same units as the data; variance has squared units.
4. Limits. With the same population variance and independent sampling, quadrupling n halves the theoretical standard error; it does not promise a smaller realized estimation error in every sample. With correlated observations, Var(X_bar) also includes (2/n^2) sum_{i<j} Cov(X_i,X_j); the independent-observation formula need not apply. A small standard error does not repair selection bias. These notes do not introduce a confidence interval or assume normality merely to derive the variance identity.

source.text:
Sampling variability: spread and precision
1. Target. Independent observations X_1,...,X_n have a common mean mu and finite variance sigma^2. The sample mean estimates mu. Standard deviation describes the spread of individual observations; the standard error of the mean describes the spread of sample means under repeated sampling.
2. Calculation. Var(X_bar) = (1/n^2) sum_i Var(X_i) = sigma^2/n under these assumptions. Hence SE(X_bar) = sigma/sqrt(n). In practice sigma is usually unknown and is estimated by s, with s^2 = sum_i (x_i-x_bar)^2/(n-1) for n>1. Then the estimated standard error is s/sqrt(n).
3. Worked data. For observations 1,3,5,7, n=4, x_bar=4 and the sum of squared deviations is 20. Thus s^2=20/3, s is about 2.582, and the estimated standard error is about 1.291. The estimated standard error is not 20/3 or s/4. Standard deviation and standard error have the same units as the data; variance has squared units.
4. Limits. With the same population variance and independent sampling, quadrupling n halves the theoretical standard error; it does not promise a smaller realized estimation error in every sample. With correlated observations, Var(X_bar) also includes (2/n^2) sum_{i<j} Cov(X_i,X_j); the independent-observation formula need not apply. A small standard error does not repair selection bias. These notes do not introduce a confidence interval or assume normality merely to derive the variance identity.
